reviews.title: Paid Users get everything, everyone else gets nothing.
reviews.body:
I've been on here since 2020, back when it was Twitter and before Elon bought it and turned the whole thing into a controversy. It's gotten harder to recommend since then. 
The biggest thing is how much the app clearly favors paid accounts now. If you're not subscribed your posts barely get seen, and it feels like the free experience exists mainly to make you want to pay. That's a choice they're allowed to make, but it makes the app noticeably worse for the majority of people using it.

It's also turned into pure rage-bait and engagement farming. Since payouts got tied to views, the whole timeline is people posting whatever will make you angry enough to reply, because arguing in the comments pays. Half of it is recycled content with a bait caption slapped on. Honestly it might be worse than Instagram at this point, which I didn't think was possible.

The reach is completely broken too. I've watched unverified accounts pull 500k views on random memes with zero context or effort behind them while I sit at barely 200 views on posts I actually put thought into. Once an account has followers the algorithm just keeps feeding it, and if you're small there's no realistic way to break out of that no matter what you post unless you pay. Smaller accounts are essentially invisible by default.

Support is the worst part. Live chat is locked behind Premium, so if you're not paying there's no real way to get anything resolved. I actually subscribed once partly to get access to support, and it still didn't help. Paying to talk to someone and then getting nowhere anyway is a bad look for an app this size. Support should be equal  and free for every account.

Having a small following doesn't mean you're a bot, a scam, or an NSFW spam account, but that's how smaller accounts get treated by default, and it's frustrating when you're a real person with a real problem and no way to prove it.

Community Notes is a genuinely good feature and one of the few things that's actually improved things, but it gets abused. Because contributors are anonymous, it turns into a way for people to take shots at posts without putting their own name on it, and you end up with notes that are less about correcting anything and more about scoring a point. When it works it's great. When it doesn't it's just anonymous sniping with an official label on it.

The other issue is the moderation. I'm moderate to right leaning myself, so this isn't a political complaint, but the platform markets itself on free speech while in practice a handful of extreme right leaning accounts set the tone for everything. They pile onto anyone who disagrees, including smaller right wing accounts who do the same or even worse sometimes, since there's an incentive to farm clips and dunks out of whoever's available. Very little actually stops it. Free speech should mean everyone gets to talk, not that the loudest and most aggressive accounts get to run people off the platform while everyone else absorbs the harassment.

The core product still works and I haven't fully left, but I use it a lot less than I used to. Between the paywalling, the rage-bait, the broken reach, the paid support that doesn't work, and the moderation, it's a worse app than the one I signed up for six years ago. Hopefully someone actually reads this and decides to change something.

reviews.body:
“When I first joined Threads, I didn’t fully understand it. The posts felt like they were speaking into the air, and it wasn’t clear who they were meant for. But after spending time reading, something shifted — I realized Threads is built to make people feel seen. It’s a place where someone says ‘Good morning,’ where someone reminds you that you matter, where someone lifts your spirit when you didn’t even know you needed it.

Threads isn’t meant for negativity, confusion, or misinterpretation. It’s meant for connection. It’s meant for encouragement. It’s meant for those little reminders that you’re not alone in the world. And once you understand that, the whole app feels different — almost like an awakening.

The only thing Threads needs is clearer instructions at the beginning, because people who are very literal might misunderstand and think every post is directed at them personally. That’s where social media can sometimes hurt people — when the purpose isn’t explained. But when you look at Threads through the lens of positivity, kindness, and community, it becomes a beautiful space.

Threads is at its best when it’s used to uplift. When it’s used to remind someone they’re great. When it’s used to say ‘I care.’ When it’s used to bring people together instead of pulling them apart.

If you use Threads with the Miracle Frequency — with love, unity, and good intention — it becomes a place where people feel supported, encouraged, and inspired. And that’s what social media should be.”

reviews.title: Broken Platform. Expected Better.
reviews.body:
My account was suspended for alleged “inauthentic activity,” and I have yet to receive any meaningful support.

I’ve submitted multiple appeals over the course of several days. Every single one has been rejected within seconds with what appears to be an automated response telling me to “log in and complete the on-screen instructions.”

The problem is that there are no on-screen instructions. My account only displays that it’s suspended in read-only mode. I can’t access the settings, I can’t change my password, and there is no recovery flow to complete. The support email is unmonitored, and the suspended account can’t even contact the official support account.

Whether the suspension itself was correct or not, the support process is broken. If users are told to complete recovery steps, those recovery steps should actually exist. At the very least, there should be a way to request a genuine manual review when the automated process fails.

I expected better from a platform this large.
